instructions.fr: Questions du prof, en anglais, sans corrigé dans les fichiers : les réponses sont **proposées** (déduites du tutoriel et du cours). Plusieurs réponses justes possibles quand l’énoncé dit « Select all correct statements ».
instructions.en: The teacher’s questions, with no official answers in the files: the answers are **proposed** (deduced from the tutorial and the course). Several answers may be correct when the statement says “Select all correct statements”.

question.fr: A selected parent P has mandatory child C. Which statement follows from the mandatory relationship?
question.en: A selected parent P has mandatory child C. Which statement follows from the mandatory relationship?

options.fr: C must be selected whenever P is selected.
options.en: C must be selected whenever P is selected.

options.fr: C must occur in every product even if P is optional and absent.
options.en: C must occur in every product even if P is optional and absent.

options.fr: The relationship defines how many users may execute C.
options.en: The relationship defines how many users may execute C.

options.fr: C must be omitted whenever P is selected.
options.en: C must be omitted whenever P is selected.

options.fr: Selecting P leaves selection of C unconstrained.
options.en: Selecting P leaves selection of C unconstrained.

explanation.fr:
**Réponse proposée : a.** *Mandatory* : si P est sélectionné, C l'est. (b) un parent optionnel absent supprime son sous-arbre.

Dans le cours : « Lines 9, 11 and 12 are the mandatory relationships between the features, meaning that their selection status must match ».

→ Revoir : ch. 3 « Les feature models », § 3.1 Ce que chaque relation permet de conclure ; ch. 3 « Les feature models », § 1.2 Le tableau de la notation
explanation.en:
**Proposed answer: a.** Mandatory: whenever P is selected, C is selected; an absent optional P removes C.

In the course: “Lines 9, 11 and 12 are the mandatory relationships between the features, meaning that their selection status must match”.

→ Review: ch. 3 “Feature models”, § 3.1 What each relationship lets you conclude; ch. 3 “Feature models”, § 1.2 The notation table

src.quote: A selected parent P has mandatory child C. Which statement follows from the mandatory relationship?

question.fr: For two features A and B, the tutorial’s Includes relationship from A to B means A requires B. Which statements hold?
question.en: For two features A and B, the tutorial’s Includes relationship from A to B means A requires B. Which statements hold?

options.fr: Selecting A entails selecting B.
options.en: Selecting A entails selecting B.

options.fr: Selecting B necessarily entails selecting A.
options.en: Selecting B necessarily entails selecting A.

options.fr: The dependency makes both features mandatory in every product.
options.en: The dependency makes both features mandatory in every product.

options.fr: Selecting A while omitting B violates the dependency.
options.en: Selecting A while omitting B violates the dependency.

options.fr: A and B cannot be selected together.
options.en: A and B cannot be selected together.

explanation.fr:
**Réponse proposée : a, d.** *Includes* de A vers B = A requires B : A sans B viole la dépendance (d), A entraîne B (a). (b) réciproque fausse ; (c), (e) faux.

Dans le cours : « If a requirement requires another requirement, for example, Images requires Rtf format, let’s proceed as follows ».

→ Revoir : ch. 3 « Les feature models », § 3.1 Ce que chaque relation permet de conclure ; ch. 3 « Les feature models », § 1.2 Le tableau de la notation
explanation.en:
**Proposed answer: a, d.** Includes from A to B means A requires B: A entails B (a) and A without B violates it (d); B does not entail A.

In the course: “If a requirement requires another requirement, for example, Images requires Rtf format, let’s proceed as follows”.

→ Review: ch. 3 “Feature models”, § 3.1 What each relationship lets you conclude; ch. 3 “Feature models”, § 1.2 The notation table

question.fr: A requirement permits between one and three child features under selected P. A modeller instead makes all three children mandatory under P. With no other constraints, which statements hold?
question.en: A requirement permits between one and three child features under selected P. A modeller instead makes all three children mandatory under P. With no other constraints, which statements hold?

options.fr: The model rejects some selections permitted by the requirement.
options.en: The model rejects some selections permitted by the requirement.

options.fr: The mandatory-child model and the requirement admit the same selections.
options.en: The mandatory-child model and the requirement admit the same selections.

options.fr: The mandatory-child model violates the upper bound of the requirement.
options.en: The mandatory-child model violates the upper bound of the requirement.

options.fr: A [1..3] group would express the stated permitted counts.
options.en: A [1..3] group would express the stated permitted counts.

options.fr: The difference can be fixed by renaming the features alone.
options.en: The difference can be fixed by renaming the features alone.

explanation.fr:
**Réponse proposée : a, d.** Tout obligatoire n'admet que la sélection {1,2,3} : on **rejette** les sélections à 1 ou 2 enfants (a). Un groupe `[1..3]` exprime les effectifs permis (d). (c) la borne haute (3) n'est pas violée ; (e) renommer n'y change rien.

Dans le cours : « Group cardinality (between m and n leaf features should be selected in a product if F0 is selected in the … ».

→ Revoir : ch. 3 « Les feature models », § 3.2 Méthode : compter les sélections permises d’un groupe
explanation.en:
**Proposed answer: a, d.** Making all three mandatory rejects the selections of one or two children that the requirement permits (a); a [1..3] group expresses the permitted counts (d).

In the course: “Group cardinality (between m and n leaf features should be selected in a product if F0 is selected in the …”.

→ Review: ch. 3 “Feature models”, § 3.2 Method: counting the selections a group allows

question.fr: A modeller adds a response-time attribute to a feature as part of the tutorial’s proposed quality extensions. Which practices help make this attribute useful?
question.en: A modeller adds a response-time attribute to a feature as part of the tutorial’s proposed quality extensions. Which practices help make this attribute useful?

options.fr: Define an allowed domain and any acceptance bound.
options.en: Define an allowed domain and any acceptance bound.

options.fr: Keep the target value distinct from evidence that an implementation meets it.
options.en: Keep the target value distinct from evidence that an implementation meets it.

options.fr: Assume that setting a value forces generated code to meet it.
options.en: Assume that setting a value forces generated code to meet it.

options.fr: Specify a unit and the conditions under which the time is measured.
options.en: Specify a unit and the conditions under which the time is measured.

options.fr: Use arbitrary numbers without units because the field is numeric.
options.en: Use arbitrary numbers without units because the field is numeric.

explanation.fr:
**Réponse proposée : a, b, d.** Un attribut utile a un domaine et des bornes d'acceptation (a), une unité et des conditions de mesure (d), et la valeur **cible** reste distincte de la preuve que l'implémentation l'atteint (b). (c) fixer une valeur dans le modèle ne garantit rien sur le code ; (e) faux.

Dans le cours : « the features are boolean in nature since they represent functional requirements, and that the non-functional requirements are of a more diverse nature ».

→ Revoir : ch. 3 « Les feature models », § 3.4 Attributs, features abstraites, cas ClothingStores
explanation.en:
**Proposed answer: a, b, d.** A useful attribute has a domain and acceptance bound (a), keeps the target distinct from evidence (b) and specifies unit and measurement conditions (d); setting a value does not make code meet it.

In the course: “the features are boolean in nature since they represent functional requirements, and that the non-functional requirements are of a more diverse nature”.

→ Review: ch. 3 “Feature models”, § 3.4 Attributes, abstract features, the ClothingStores case

question.fr: A selected parent has exactly three child features A, B and C in a [1..2] group. There are no other constraints or attributes. How many distinct child-selection sets are allowed?
question.en: A selected parent has exactly three child features A, B and C in a [1..2] group. There are no other constraints or attributes. How many distinct child-selection sets are allowed?

options.fr: Seven.
options.en: Seven.

options.fr: Eight.
options.en: Eight.

options.fr: Six.
options.en: Six.

options.fr: Three.
options.en: Three.

options.fr: Two.
options.en: Two.

explanation.fr:
**Réponse proposée : c.** `[1..2]` parmi 3 : C(3,1) + C(3,2) = 3 + 3 = **6** (vérifié).

Dans le cours : « Group cardinality (between m and n leaf features should be selected in a product if F0 is selected in the … ».

→ Revoir : ch. 3 « Les feature models », § 3.2 Méthode : compter les sélections permises d’un groupe
explanation.en:
**Proposed answer: c.** [1..2] among three children: C(3,1) + C(3,2) = 3 + 3 = 6 selections.

In the course: “Group cardinality (between m and n leaf features should be selected in a product if F0 is selected in the …”.

→ Review: ch. 3 “Feature models”, § 3.2 Method: counting the selections a group allows

question.fr: A requires B and B requires C. Assume no other constraints. Which statements follow?
question.en: A requires B and B requires C. Assume no other constraints. Which statements follow?

options.fr: Selecting C entails selecting A.
options.en: Selecting C entails selecting A.

options.fr: Omitting A forces B and C to be omitted.
options.en: Omitting A forces B and C to be omitted.

options.fr: The dependencies prohibit selecting A, B and C together.
options.en: The dependencies prohibit selecting A, B and C together.

options.fr: Selecting A entails selecting C.
options.en: Selecting A entails selecting C.

options.fr: Selecting B without A can be valid if C is selected.
options.en: Selecting B without A can be valid if C is selected.

explanation.fr:
**Réponse proposée : d, e.** Transitivité : A ⇒ B et B ⇒ C donnent A ⇒ C (d). B sans A est valide si C est choisi (e). (a) C n'entraîne pas A ; (b) ¬A ne force rien ; (c) A, B, C ensemble sont permis.

Dans le cours : « Requires (F2 is required by F1) ».

→ Revoir : ch. 3 « Les feature models », § 3.1 Ce que chaque relation permet de conclure
explanation.en:
**Proposed answer: d, e.** Transitivity: A entails C (d). B without A is valid if C is selected (e). C does not entail A and omitting A forces nothing.

In the course: “Requires (F2 is required by F1)”.

→ Review: ch. 3 “Feature models”, § 3.1 What each relationship lets you conclude

src.quote: A requires B and B requires C. Assume no other constraints. Which statements follow?
Requires (F2 is required by F1)

question.fr: Text alignment is selected. Its Align attribute is a set of distinct values from {Left,Right,Center,Justify}, with [1..4]. Ignore all other choices. How many distinct sets of supported alignment modes exist?
question.en: Text alignment is selected. Its Align attribute is a set of distinct values from {Left,Right,Center,Justify}, with [1..4]. Ignore all other choices. How many distinct sets of supported alignment modes exist?

options.fr: Four.
options.en: Four.

options.fr: One.
options.en: One.

options.fr: Fifteen.
options.en: Fifteen.

options.fr: Twenty-four.
options.en: Twenty-four.

options.fr: Sixteen.
options.en: Sixteen.

explanation.fr:
**Réponse proposée : c.** `[1..4]` parmi 4 valeurs distinctes : 2⁴ − 1 = **15** (vérifié).

Dans le cours : « we can indicate the range [1..4] to mean that each text editor of the product line could have between 1 … ».

→ Revoir : ch. 3 « Les feature models », § 3.2 Méthode : compter les sélections permises d’un groupe
explanation.en:
**Proposed answer: c.** [1..4] among four distinct values: 2⁴ − 1 = 15 non-empty sets.

In the course: “we can indicate the range [1..4] to mean that each text editor of the product line could have between 1 …”.

→ Review: ch. 3 “Feature models”, § 3.2 Method: counting the selections a group allows

question.fr: Use this local fragment of ClothingStores: Shop is optional under the root; Cart is mandatory under Shop; selected Shop requires [1..2] of Online payment and Offline payment. Ignore all other constraints. Which statements hold?
question.en: Use this local fragment of ClothingStores: Shop is optional under the root; Cart is mandatory under Shop; selected Shop requires [1..2] of Online payment and Offline payment. Ignore all other constraints. Which statements hold?

options.fr: Shop with Cart and Online payment alone satisfies this fragment.
options.en: Shop with Cart and Online payment alone satisfies this fragment.

options.fr: Shop with Cart and both payment methods satisfies this fragment.
options.en: Shop with Cart and both payment methods satisfies this fragment.

options.fr: Shop without Cart satisfies the fragment if both payment methods are selected.
options.en: Shop without Cart satisfies the fragment if both payment methods are selected.

options.fr: Shop with Cart but neither payment method satisfies the fragment.
options.en: Shop with Cart but neither payment method satisfies the fragment.

options.fr: Omitting Shop and all its descendants satisfies this fragment.
options.en: Omitting Shop and all its descendants satisfies this fragment.

explanation.fr:
**Réponse proposée : a, b, e.** Shop est optionnel : l'omettre avec tous ses descendants satisfait le fragment (e). Si Shop est choisi : Cart obligatoire et `[1..2]` paiements ; (a) un seul paiement, (b) les deux conviennent. (c) sans Cart, non ; (d) aucun paiement, non.

Dans le cours : « Line 10 defines the optional relationship obligating the parent to be present if the child feature is selected, but not the opposite » ; « Lines 9, 11 and 12 are the mandatory relationships between the features, meaning that their selection status must match ».

explanation.en:
**Proposed answer: a, b, e.** Shop is optional, so omitting it with its descendants satisfies the fragment (e); if Shop is chosen, Cart is mandatory and [1..2] payments are needed (a, b).

In the course: “Line 10 defines the optional relationship obligating the parent to be present if the child feature is selected, but not the opposite”; “Lines 9, 11 and 12 are the mandatory relationships between the features, meaning that their selection status must match”.

→ Review: ch. 3 “Feature models”, § 3.3 Reading a model fragment

question.fr: List is selected. Its children Alphabetic, Numeric and Vignette form [1..3]. Alphabetic, when selected, must support [1..2] of Upper and Lower. Numeric and Vignette are omitted. Which selections for Alphabetic’s supported types are valid?
question.en: List is selected. Its children Alphabetic, Numeric and Vignette form [1..3]. Alphabetic, when selected, must support [1..2] of Upper and Lower. Numeric and Vignette are omitted. Which selections for Alphabetic’s supported types are valid?

options.fr: Upper only.
options.en: Upper only.

options.fr: No type.
options.en: No type.

options.fr: Roman only.
options.en: Roman only.

options.fr: Lower only.
options.en: Lower only.

options.fr: Upper and Lower.
options.en: Upper and Lower.

explanation.fr:
**Réponse proposée : a, d, e.** Seul Alphabetic est choisi ; il faut `[1..2]` parmi Upper et Lower : Upper seul (a), Lower seul (d), les deux (e). « Aucun type » viole `[1..2]` (b) ; Roman appartient à Numeric (c).

Dans le cours : « Those systems of the text editor product line that include the Alphabetic list feature must provide the user with the … ».

→ Revoir : ch. 3 « Les feature models », § 3.3 Lire un fragment de modèle
explanation.en:
**Proposed answer: a, d, e.** Only Alphabetic is chosen (the group needs at least one child); [1..2] of Upper and Lower allows Upper only (a), Lower only (d), or both (e).

In the course: “Those systems of the text editor product line that include the Alphabetic list feature must provide the user with the …”.

→ Review: ch. 3 “Feature models”, § 3.3 Reading a model fragment
